title: Conversation Slices — rough PRD & idea pad
body:
Purpose / elevator:
Allow apps to opt into storing and referencing small, indexed chunks of prior conversation ("slices") that are addressable, compressible, and billed separately. Goal is to reduce token usage for long-lived multimodal chat sessions while keeping user control and predictable costs.

Motivation / problems we see:
- Apps keep sending entire session or very long context to maintain continuity — expensive and brittle.
- Full-session caching doesn't handle edits or partial references (user says "remember the blue logo from two messages ago").
- Customers want predictable cost controls for persistent contexts (e.g., 30-day active history).
- Server-side naive caching leads to stale or privacy-unfriendly behavior; need explicit opt-in UX and TTL semantics.

Proposed feature (high-level):
- Concept: Conversation Slice = a named, appendable fragment tied to a session/user. Small-ish (1–2k tokens typical) and versioned.
- API: CRUD ops + attach-by-ref in prompts. Example: create_slice(session_id, name, content, metadata), update_slice(slice_id, patch), list_slices(session_id), get_slice(slice_id), delete_slice(slice_id).
- When calling generation, clients can pass slice_refs: [slice_id@rev] with hinting (weight, inline-priority). Runtime will resolve to either inline expansion, compressed embedding, or a small KV reference depending on routing policy.
- Billing: slices have storage cost + retrieval cost (per-resolve tokens or fixed retrieval charge). Option for aggregation billing when multiple slices are pulled inside same request window.

User stories (rough):
- As a chat product engineer, I want to store a "user-profile" slice so subsequent messages can reference attributes without re-sending them each time.
- As a support agent app, I want to attach a "case-summary" slice that is auto-generated from transcripts and used only for rerank/rerank-with-knowledge flows.
- As a privacy/offboarding admin, I want to delete user slices when retention policy triggers and ensure they are not cache-eligible afterwards.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- create_slice and get_slice APIs implemented; slices stored and retrievable by id.
- Generation API accepts slice_refs and expands slice text inline when policy = inline.
- Basic UI card in Console: list slices for a customer, show size, last-updated, and TTL.
- Billing meter emits slice-storage and slice-retrieval lines for observability.

Edge-case UX / behaviours:
- If slice referenced but marked private/inaccessible -> engine falls back to client-provided short summary or omits. Must be explicit; do not silently leak.
- Conflict resolution: slices are versioned; updates produce new rev ids. Clients can optionally request optimistic-merge semantics.

Implementation options (tradeoffs):
1) Inline-first: always expand slice text into prompt (simple, predictable cost) — bad for very long slices.
2) Embedding-backed: store compressed embedding and use similarity + soft prompting to rehydrate small text — saves tokens but harder to guarantee exactness and harder to support patch/edits.
3) Hybrid: if slice size < threshold expand inline; otherwise use embedding retrieval + optional pinned summary stored with slice. This seems most pragmatic for MVP.

Storage model thoughts:
- store original text + generated canonical summary + embedding + metadata (owner, TTL, tags, access lists).
- retention/TTL enforcement as background job with audit logs.
- encrypted at rest (KMS/HSM integration required for Private deployments).

Console / UX sketch (notes):
- Row per slice: name | kind (profile/summary/context) | size | last updated | ttl | attached routes (which apps use it) | delete/archive action.
- Drawer: preview content, show history / revisions, quick attach button that returns slice_ref string for client SDK.
- Quick-create from transcript: selection -> "Create slice from selection" -> auto-suggest name + summary.

API examples (informal):
- POST /v1/slices { session_id, name, content, ttl_days, visibility } -> { slice_id, rev }
- POST /v1/generate { prompt, slice_refs:[{id,rev,weight}], model, policies } -> streamed token response
- SDK: client.slices.create(...) client.chat.generate({sliceRefs: [...]})

Monitoring / metrics needed:
- slices.created, slices.deleted, slices.retrieved, slices.size_distribution
- token-saved estimate per-retrieval (for ROI) — compare baseline tokens vs actual tokens used after slice expansion
- errors: unauthorized-slice-access, slice-not-found

Security & compliance considerations:
- slices might contain PII; need per-slice data classification and redaction helpers.
- allow enterprise customers to scope slices to VPC/Private partitions (no cross-tenant leakage).
- retention policies must be enforceable for Private deployments with on-prem storage.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (experiments): internal-only flag for inline-expand; no billing. Test with 3 internal apps.
- Phase 1 (MVP public): API + console listing + basic billing and TTL. Enable for Hosted API customers opt-in.
- Phase 2 (optimizations): embedding-backed retrieval, compression profiles, per-route retrieval policies, analytics.

Open questions / unknowns (todo):
- Pricing model: per-slice-month + per-retrieval-token? flat retrieval fee? need finance input.
- How to index slices for fast resolution in high-QPS workloads? (hot path vs cold path segregation)
- Garbage collection: who triggers and how to handle cascade deletes across rollouts?
- SDK ergonomics: do we expose slice lifecycle helpers in first-party SDKs or leave as REST primitives?

Next steps / immediate todos: 
- Sync with Applied ML on embedding vs summary tradeoffs (Kai).
- Ask Console team for low-fidelity card + attach UX (Maya).
- Spreadsheet with pricing scenarios and cost simulations (estimate storage and retrieval volumes).
- Quick internal test harness: instrument 2 internal chatbots to use slices and measure token reductions across 2 weeks.

Notes to self: keep feature simple for first iteration. Prioritise clear semantics (TTL, visibility, deletion) over fancy retrieval heuristics. Document failure modes for customers (e.g., slice stale, unauthorized) so integrators can degrade gracefully.

-- oliver
